subject: Re: Competitive bake-off: Acme evaluation & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed bake-off plan (Acme)

Hi Lisa,

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our end and suggested next steps so we stay aligned on scope and success criteria for the competitive bake-off: 

What we heard from you:
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost and tail latency for your customer-facing chat product while preserving output quality (safety + hallucination targets).
- Baseline: currently running on Hyperscale-S API (gpt-3.5-ish equivalent) with average p95 latency ~420ms and token cost you quoted.
- Key tests you care about: latency (p50/p95), 99th percentile latency under load, throughput (tokens/sec), token-level cost, and sample-quality parity on your 200-case prompt set.

Proposed bake-off plan (high level):
1) Test matrix: Hyperscale-S (current), Hyperscale-L (higher perf), Redwood-open-quant (our recommended variant), and Redwood-managed-highmem (dedicated config).
2) Success criteria: match or beat p95 latency by 15% and stay within 10% quality delta on your prompt set; cost savings target 20%+ at target throughput.
3) Timeline: kickoff this week, data and eval prompts by Wed 10/07, infra access + S3 read by Fri 10/09, 1-week run of automated load tests 10/12-10/16.
4) Owners: Redwood AE (me) for coordination, Aditya (SE) for infra/setup and test harness, Ben (CS) for rollout/observability integrations.

I attached a first-pass test plan and our performance matrix for reference. Can you confirm: a) the prompt set we should use (is the 200-case set on the shared Drive the canonical one?), and b) whether Rahul should own the infra access for provisioning (we'll need an S3 bucket + temp creds for telemetry ingestion)?

If that looks good I'll schedule the kickoff and loop in our infra ops person.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: acme-bakeoff-test-plan-v1.pdf, redwood-performance-matrix.xlsx
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed bake-off plan (Acme)

Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications: 
1) Prompt set: yes, the 200-case set in the shared Drive (folder "Acme-eval/prompt-set-v3") is the canonical one. I'll share folder-level permissions for the account alias: acme-eval@acme.com.
2) Infra owner: Rahul will own the provisioning. He can stand up an S3 bucket and provide an IAM role for Redwood to stream telemetry. He's cc'd here and will follow up with specifics.
3) Success criteria: the 10% quality delta, just to be explicit, that should be measured by your automated eval (BLEU/ROUGE + our human-reviewed subset) and we'll define the threshold rubric before running.

Next actions: please send a kickoff invite and list of exact credentials/permissions you need. We can commit to the 10/12-10/16 window for the run.

Best,
Lisa Chen | Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed bake-off plan (Acme)

Hey Rahul / team,

Quick technical checklist from my side to make the infra handoff smooth: 
- S3 bucket name + region (we prefer us-west-2 for latency parity).
- IAM role with GetObject and PutObject for a temporary telemetry prefix (we'll only write aggregated telemetry, not raw logs).
- Optional: a small sample dataset (10 threads) with PII redacted so we can sanity-check parsing and rate-limiting behavior before full run.
- If you want us to hit your Hyperscale endpoints, please provide a test API key + rate limits so we can include them in the same harness.

I'll create the Jenkins job and the load-test config once I have the bucket name and the API key. I also wired up a simple script that will compute p50/p95/99 and token-cost breakouts; I'll share that in the Drive link.

Aditya
Aditya Rao | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
